chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Wuhayb ibn Ḥafṣ, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, he said:

I asked him about a man who performed salat (prayer) while there was urine or janabah on his garment. He said: whether he knew of it or did not know, he must repeat it, meaning the repetition of the salat (prayer).

If he came to know, then the correct way regarding his statement, 'whether he knew of it or did not know,' is that what is intended is his state at the time he began the salat (prayer), after knowledge had already previously come to him. For whenever prior knowledge of the occurrence of the impurity had been established and he then forgot, repetition is required of him, as we have explained; and what follows further clarifies that.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual prayer under discussion
key_terms.النَّجَاسَةِ: ritual impurity present on the garment
key_terms.الْإِعَادَةُ: the obligation of repeating the act, here the salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْعِلْمُ: knowledge or awareness of the impurity
key_terms.بَوْلٌ: urine, a source of ritual impurity
key_terms.ثَوْبِهِ: his garment or clothing in which the salat (prayer) was performed
key_terms.جَنَابَةٌ: janabah, a state or source associated with major ritual impurity

ai.seo_question: Must salat (prayer) be repeated if someone prayed in clothing containing impurity?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling of performing salat (prayer) in a garment affected by najasah such as urine or janabah. It indicates the obligation of repeating the salat (prayer), and the appended clarification explains the ruling in connection with prior knowledge of the impurity followed by forgetfulness.
